title: What is Political Theory?

cards.h: Every question in Paper I starts here
cards.b:
Before you study Plato, Rawls or Marx, you need to know what "political theory" even is. UPSC asks about this directly, and the ideas here come back in almost every answer you write.

Political theory is the systematic thinking about political life. It asks big questions: Who should rule? Why should we obey? What is a just society? What is freedom?

Normative theory asks what should be. Plato's ideal state and Rawls's theory of justice are normative.

Empirical theory asks what is. It studies how voters actually behave or how parties actually win. David Easton and Robert Dahl worked this way.

Andrew Hacker

Political theory is a mix of two things: a search for knowledge about politics (science) and a search for the best political order (philosophy).

George Sabine

Political theory is "disciplined investigation of political problems". He saw it as the history of how thinkers answered the problems of their own times.

David Held

It is a network of concepts and generalisations about political life, covering ideas about government, state and society.

• Explain. It tells us why things happen, such as why revolutions break out.
  • Evaluate. It judges institutions against values, such as asking whether a law is just.
  • Prescribe. It suggests what we should do, such as how to make democracy deeper.

Good UPSC answers show all three. Don't only describe a thinker; say what their idea explains and where it falls short.

Political thought

The ideas of a person or a society at a given time, such as Gandhian thought.

Political philosophy

The most abstract level. It asks about the nature of the good life and of justice.

Political ideology

A set of ideas meant to drive action, such as liberalism or socialism. It wants to change the world, not just explain it.

Political science

The study of politics using scientific methods and data.
In the 1950s, many scholars said political theory was dying. Most new work was just history of old ideas, and the scientific study of politics was taking over.

David Easton, 1953

In The Political System, he said theory had become mere history of ideas. It was not producing new theory that could guide research.

Alfred Cobban, 1953

In his essay "The Decline of Political Theory", he blamed academics for turning away from real political problems.

Peter Laslett, 1956

He famously wrote that "for the moment, anyway, political philosophy is dead". He blamed logical positivism, which said value statements were meaningless.

Isaiah Berlin answered back in his 1962 essay "Does Political Theory Still Exist?". He said that as long as people disagree about ends, such as liberty vs equality, political theory will exist. Only in a world where everyone agreed on goals would it die.

"Political theory is a branch of moral philosophy."
Isaiah Berlin, Two Concepts of Liberty (1958)

Leo Strauss and Hannah Arendt also defended the classical tradition.

Then in 1971, John Rawls published A Theory of Justice. It is widely seen as the moment normative theory came roaring back.

cards.h: The end of ideology, history and old methods
cards.b:
Daniel Bell, 1960

In The End of Ideology, Bell argued that the West had settled its big ideological fights. Welfare capitalism had won, so grand political visions were exhausted. Critics said this was itself an ideology.

Quentin Skinner and the Cambridge School

Skinner's essay "Meaning and Understanding in the History of Ideas" (1969) said we must read old texts in their own context, as moves in the debates of their time. With J.G.A. Pocock and John Dunn, this gave the history of political thought new rigour.

Francis Fukuyama, 1989

His essay "The End of History?" (a book in 1992) claimed liberal democracy was the final form of government. Ethnic wars, 9/11 and China's rise showed the debate was far from over.

Indian debates show theory is alive. Think about reservation (equality vs merit), sedition law (order vs liberty), or the Uniform Civil Code (equality vs group rights).

Ambedkar's question in the Constituent Assembly, about political democracy without social democracy, is a normative question. Ending an answer with an Indian example like this lifts your marks.

"Comment: Political theory is dead." (a common style)
"Discuss the relevance of normative political theory today."

Structure: define theory, show the 1950s decline argument with names and years, show the revival through Berlin and Rawls, then end with how new areas like feminism, multiculturalism and green theory keep it alive.

quiz.q: Who wrote that political philosophy was "dead" in 1956?
quiz.w: Peter Laslett wrote this in his introduction to Philosophy, Politics and Society (1956).

quiz.q: Normative political theory mainly deals with…
quiz.w: Normative theory is about values and ideals: what ought to be.

quiz.q: Which 1971 book is credited with reviving normative theory?
quiz.w: John Rawls's A Theory of Justice (1971) is the landmark revival text.

quiz.q: Isaiah Berlin argued political theory survives because…
quiz.w: As long as people disagree about ends like liberty and equality, political theory lives.

quiz.q: Which school said value statements were meaningless, hurting political philosophy?
quiz.w: Logical positivism held only empirically verifiable statements were meaningful.

quiz.q: Who wrote 'The Decline of Political Theory' (1953)?
The Cambridge School's key method is to read texts…
o: In their historical and linguistic context
quiz.w: Skinner, Pocock and Dunn read texts as moves in the debates of their time.

quiz.q: The End of Ideology (1960) was written by…
Proposing how to make democracy deeper is an example of which job?
A set of ideas meant to drive political action is best called…
quiz.w: Ideology aims to change the world, not just explain it.
